I added a 0.25s pause between sandbox calls in `tests/test_payments.py`:

- **`SANDBOX_CALL_INTERVAL = 0.25`** is a new constant with a comment pointing to the 5 requests/second limit. A gap of 0.2s is the minimum; the extra 0.05s gives some headroom.
- **`test_charges_roundtrip`** now waits that long before each request except the first, so the test is only about 0.75s slower.

I haven't run the test because it calls the real sandbox, so I can't confirm yet that the CI flakes are gone. One limit: this only spaces out calls within this one test. If other tests or parallel CI jobs hit the sandbox at the same time, they could still go over the limit together. If that happens, the next step would be retrying when the sandbox returns 429 (its "too many requests" error).

I also saved the 5 requests/second limit to EngramDB as a project memory so it comes up when someone writes future sandbox tests.
